profile.research_note:
Reused from operator-level research completed in an earlier phase of this project (twoai_dc_operators row: Crown Castle Fiber, operator-level status: exhausted).

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Crown Castle Fiber was the fiber connectivity and colocation-adjacent business line of Crown Castle International Corp., the publicly traded tower and communications infrastructure company. In March 2025, Crown Castle announced it would sell its Fiber Solutions business, comprising approximately 90,000 route miles of fiber, to Zayo Group for about 4.25 billion dollars, while its Small Cells business was sold separately to EQTs Active Core Infrastructure fund, for a combined transaction value of 8.5 billion dollars. Subsequent reporting indicates the transaction closed in 2026, with Crown Castle emerging as a pure-play tower company no longer operating fiber or small cell businesses, and Zayo taking over the Fiber Solutions assets that included the Crown Castle Fiber brand. This registry could not independently confirm the precise disposition of the specific Maryland facility recorded under the Crown Castle Fiber name, so its research status is marked exhausted rather than complete, and it is flagged as a former_operator lead for the facility-research phase: any facility still attributed to Crown Castle Fiber in this registry most likely now operates under Zayo Group and should be reconciled accordingly rather than assumed to remain a Crown Castle asset. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

reading.body:
This facility publishes no power capacity figure. Its research status is exhausted because Crown Castle Fiber, the operator of record, sold its fiber solutions business to Zayo Group in 2026, and this registry cannot confirm whether the Baltimore asset transferred with that sale or remains under different ownership. Any assessment of this campus's relevance to AI infrastructure depends on confirming current operator and published specifications, which are not available.

Maryland has 11 mapped data center facilities but only 3 publish power capacity. This campus is the fourth-ranked by published megawatts among those three, though it contributes no figure to that ranking itself. The state's three publishing facilities together represent 9.3 megawatts of disclosed IT capacity, placing Maryland well outside the geographies where published data center build-out for AI is concentrated.

Without current operator confirmation and published power specifications, this campus cannot be assessed for relevance to AI infrastructure scaling. The site should be reconciled under Zayo Group if the asset transferred, or its current operator should be identified, before power capacity and grid position can be evaluated.
